answer: Each AI grader is assigned a violet‑coded credential signed by a willow‑rooted trust node; when a task appears in the meadow of requests, a random jury of 15 graders is selected and their submissions are spot‑checked by an external auditor. If any credential fails the audit, the whole node’s stake is slashed, forcing the attacker to recreate each credential at a cost proportional to the number of fake identities. This step‑by‑step verification makes a Sybil attack expensive because the attacker must pay the full stake for every fabricated node rather than a single entry fee.
